content.title: Second Derivatives of Parametric Curves
content.overview: In AP Calculus BC, finding the second derivative of a parametric curve is a multi-step process that measures the rate of change of the slope (dy/dx) with respect to x. Unlike the first derivative, the second derivative is not simply the second derivative of y divided by the second derivative of x. Instead, it requires differentiating the first derivative with respect to the parameter t and then normalizing that rate by dividing by dx/dt.
learning_objectives: Calculate the first derivative dy/dx for a curve defined by parametric equations x(t) and y(t).
Apply the parametric second derivative formula to find d²y/dx².
Interpret the second derivative to determine the concavity of a parametric curve at a specific point or time t.

sections.title: The Parametric Second Derivative Formula
sections.content: To find the second derivative of y with respect to x for a curve defined by x = f(t) and y = g(t), we must use the Chain Rule. First, recall that the first derivative is dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt). To find the second derivative, d²y/dx², we differentiate dy/dx with respect to t and then divide by dx/dt. Mathematically, this is expressed as: d²y/dx² = [d/dt (dy/dx)] / (dx/dt). This ensures we are finding the change in slope per unit change in x, rather than per unit change in t.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Procedure
sections.content:
1. Find dx/dt and dy/dt from the given parametric equations.
2. Calculate the first derivative dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt). This expression will usually be in terms of t.
3. Differentiate the resulting expression for dy/dx with respect to t. This gives you d/dt(dy/dx).
4. Divide this new expression by the original dx/dt. Do not forget this final division; it is the most common source of error.

![A linear flow chart showing the steps: 1. Find dx/dt and dy/dt. 2. Calculate dy/dx. 3. Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t. 4. Divide by dx/dt to get d²y/dx².](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/565b31b4-cb6d-45be-a81d-6bafa50abe62-1786526321015-641.webp)

sections.title: Concavity and the Second Derivative
sections.content: The sign of d²y/dx² determines the concavity of the graph in the xy-plane. If d²y/dx² > 0, the curve is concave up. If d²y/dx² < 0, the curve is concave down. Note that the parameter t often represents time, but the concavity describes the geometric shape of the path in the Cartesian plane.

worked_examples.question: A particle moves along a curve defined by x(t) = t² + 3t and y(t) = t³ - t. Find the second derivative d²y/dx² at t = 1.
worked_examples.solution:
Step 1: Find the first derivatives with respect to t.
dx/dt = 2t + 3
dy/dt = 3t² - 1

Step 2: Find the first derivative dy/dx.
dy/dx = (3t² - 1) / (2t + 3)

Step 3: Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t using the Quotient Rule.
d/dt [(3t² - 1) / (2t + 3)] = [(6t)(2t + 3) - (2)(3t² - 1)] / (2t + 3)²
At t = 1: [(6)(5) - (2)(2)] / (5)² = (30 - 4) / 25 = 26/25

Step 4: Divide by dx/dt.
d²y/dx² = [d/dt(dy/dx)] / (dx/dt)
At t = 1, dx/dt = 2(1) + 3 = 5.
d²y/dx² = (26/25) / 5 = 26/125.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide by dx/dt in the final step of the formula.
Errors in applying the Quotient Rule when differentiating dy/dx with respect to t.
Confusing the sign of dy/dt (vertical direction of motion) with the sign of d²y/dx² (concavity).
exam_tips: Always write out the formula d²y/dx² = [d/dt(dy/dx)] / (dx/dt) before plugging in values to avoid skipping the final division.
If the question asks for concavity, evaluate the sign of the second derivative at the specific t-value provided.
Keep your expressions in terms of t as long as possible before substituting numerical values to ensure accuracy in differentiation.
content.recap: The second derivative of a parametric curve measures concavity in the xy-plane. It is calculated by taking the derivative of the first derivative (dy/dx) with respect to the parameter t and dividing that result by dx/dt.

knowledge_claims.content: The first derivative of a parametric curve is given by dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt), provided dx/dt is not zero.
The second derivative of a parametric curve is calculated using the formula d²y/dx² = [d/dt (dy/dx)] / (dx/dt).
To find the second derivative of a parametric curve, one must first express the first derivative dy/dx as a function of the parameter t.
It is a common error to calculate the second derivative as (d²y/dt²) / (d²x/dt²); this does not yield d²y/dx².
A positive value for the parametric second derivative d²y/dx² indicates that the curve is concave up at that point in the xy-plane.
A negative value for the parametric second derivative d²y/dx² indicates that the curve is concave down at that point in the xy-plane.
The final step in finding d²y/dx² must always involve dividing the derivative of the slope by dx/dt.
The derivative d/dt(dy/dx) represents the rate of change of the curve's slope with respect to the parameter t.
If dy/dx is constant with respect to t, the second derivative d²y/dx² will be zero, indicating a linear relationship in the xy-plane.
When differentiating dy/dx with respect to t, the Quotient Rule is frequently required if dy/dx is a ratio of two functions of t.
The second derivative d²y/dx² is a measure of how the slope of the tangent line changes as x increases.
In the context of parametric motion, dx/dt represents the horizontal component of the velocity vector.

items.stem: Which procedure or value is mathematically consistent in “AP Calculus BC — Second Derivatives of Parametric Curves — Practice Record 01”?

options.A: Second Derivatives of Parametric Curves: A parametric second derivative differentiates dy/dx with respect to the parameter and divides by dx/dt again.
options.B: Integral and p-Series Tests: Positive decreasing terms may be compared with an improper integral, and a p-series converges exactly when its exponent exceeds one.
options.C: Algebraic Evaluation of Limits: Direct substitution works when expressions are continuous; indeterminate forms may require factoring, rationalizing, or equivalent algebraic restructuring.
options.D: Chain Rule: The derivative of a composite function multiplies the derivative of the outer function evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

items.explanation: Choice A is best because A parametric second derivative differentiates dy/dx with respect to the parameter and divides by dx/dt again. The other options invoke different atomic topics and do not satisfy the record's stated target as directly.

items.stem: Which relationship connects the verbal and symbolic information in “AP Calculus BC — Second Derivatives of Parametric Curves — Practice Record 02”?

options.A: Comparison and Limit Comparison Tests: Positive-term series can inherit convergence or divergence from a benchmark through inequalities or a finite positive ratio limit.
options.B: Second Derivatives of Parametric Curves: A parametric second derivative differentiates dy/dx with respect to the parameter and divides by dx/dt again.
options.C: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem: Continuity at a point requires an existing limit equal to the function value, and the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees attained values under interval continuity.
options.D: Implicit Differentiation: When variables are related implicitly, differentiating both sides with respect to the independent variable introduces derivative factors for dependent-variable terms.
